{"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the exact Upload signature, reuses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves Add, and avoids unrelated retry machinery changes. It is not fully compliant because it duplicates Add’s request/response path instead of delegating to Add and omits required validation/source-reader-error tests.","reasons":["B’s public API exactly matches Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption). A instead introduces FilesUploadOption, violating the required signature and changing option semantics.","B uses the established multipartbody.NewFile helper with field \"file\" and passes the returned replayable *bytes.Reader to the existing transport.","A explicitly adds association options and multipart fields, despite the contract prohibiting association fields and requiring FilesOption behavior to remain unchanged.","A refactors RawClient retry and body-closing behavior, an expressly out-of-scope change with broad SDK-wide semantic risk; B leaves retry machinery untouched and solves replayability locally by buffering the upload body."],"risks_a":["Upload does not have the mandated FilesOption signature.","Adds prohibited association APIs and duplicate multipart-field machinery.","Changes RawClient handling of arbitrary io.ReadSeeker bodies and ownership/closing semantics across the SDK, creating concurrency and lifecycle risks around a shared seeker in GetBody closures and exceeding scope discipline strongly demanded by contract/context (localized Files.Upload fix). Actually contract explicitly prohibits refactor unrelated retry machinery, and A does that rather than just new Upload. It also claims Add behavior preservation but modifies effective retry behavior for Add; frozen says preserve Add existing behavior/signature (though user asks report retry? Contract says Upload solution). It does not call Add, duplicates internal request path. Tests source-reader error absent too. Association tests scope. Some tests use RetryPolicy but no RetryAllMethods true? Hmm POST retry defaults perhaps policy retries? Task user says enabled RetryAllMethods. Both test policies omit RetryAllMethods. Existing defaults perhaps MaxAttempts makes all? Frozen says when retries enabled. Hidden behavior passed. Need specific visible. A test TestRawClient_Do_RetriesSeekableBodyOnRateLimit also omits RetryAllMethods; if POST retry gate passed maybe default policy retry all? Can't infer. Don't claim. In risks_b source-reader failure test absent; validation has combined error, does pre-request. Route Add violation. Retry test doesn't verify body on second attempt. Also changelog claim os.File "] 
,"risks_b":["Upload reimplements Add’s option application, Raw.Do call, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing the encoded body through Add as required; this can drift from Add semantics later.","Tests do not cover source-reader failures, and validation tests for empty filename and nil content are missing.","The retry test counts attempts but does not read or compare the multipart body on both attempts, so it does not directly verify streamed content was resent intact."]}
